name: Vigilant Vole
description: Lightweight self-hosted uptime monitor in a single Rust binary with SQLite. 30 monitor types (HTTP, ping, DNS, TCP, databases, game servers and more), 24 notification providers plus Apprise, status pages, remote agents, a REST API and config as code.

app_vars.name: var_mode
app_vars.label: Install
app_vars.help: server: the web UI and database. agent: a remote probe that runs checks for another Vigilant Vole server and reports back (no web UI; defaults to 256 MB RAM and a 1 GB disk)

app_vars.name: var_setup_token
app_vars.label: Setup Token (VV_SETUP_TOKEN)
app_vars.help: Server only: require /setup?token=<value> for the first-run setup page. Empty means off

app_vars.name: var_agent_server
app_vars.label: Agent: Server URL
app_vars.help: Agent only, required: the URL of your Vigilant Vole server, e.g. https://status.example.com

app_vars.name: var_agent_token
app_vars.label: Agent: Token
app_vars.help: Agent only, required: the vva_... token from Settings → Remote agents → New agent on the server (shown once)

app_vars.name: var_agent_name
app_vars.label: Agent: Name
app_vars.help: Agent only: the name the server shows. Empty means the container's hostname

notes.text: No default login: open the web UI right after install and create the admin account in the setup wizard. Until then anyone who can reach the page can create it.

The setup wizard needs a setup token: set one (var_setup_token, or VV_SETUP_TOKEN in /etc/vigilant-vole/vigilant-vole.env) and open /setup?token=<value>, or read the one the app logs at start (journalctl -u vigilant-vole).

The script asks whether to install the server or a remote agent (var_mode=agent). An agent needs the server URL and a token from Settings → Remote agents on that server. It runs vigilant-vole-agent.service with its settings in /etc/vigilant-vole/agent.env (mode 0600), has no web UI and defaults to 1 CPU, 256 MB RAM and a 1 GB disk.
